chunks: And by this chain, he said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when it was the month of Ramadan, would not speak except with supplication, glorification, seeking forgiveness, and glorification (Takbeer). So when he broke his fast, he said: 'O Allah, if You will, You do it.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say when breaking his fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the profound spiritual discipline of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), who practiced 'silence of the tongue' to preserve the heart for divine remembrance during Ramadan. His post-fast supplication, 'If You will, You do,' reflects the Shia theological emphasis on *tawakkul* (trust in God) and the acceptance of divine decree, linking personal piety with cosmic submission.
